1	You are diagnosing a problem in a system: an organization, a technical system, or both. Use only the evidence in this task and the evidence you choose to collect. Do not use outside facts about real organizations, and do not invent evidence.

3	Evidence collection. The initial evidence below is free. The catalogue lists further evidence you may collect: interviews, records, logs, data extracts, documents, observations. Each item is costly to collect, and **you may collect at most 3 items**. This limit is a hard constraint, like an agreed data-request scope; do not exceed it. To collect an item, use the Read tool on its file path, exactly as listed. Do not read anything else. You may collect items one at a time and decide what to collect next from what you have learned. You may also stop early, or collect nothing, if further evidence is unlikely to change your answers.
4	
5	Answer semantics:
6	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
7	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
8	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
9	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to the action you rank highest, where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
10	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.
11	
12	Answer using the initial evidence and only the items you collected. Where the evidence you have does not settle an item, answer accordingly (often "unknown" or "insufficient").

Then write a brief of at most 200 words addressed to the person who asked for the diagnosis: what is going on, how sure you are, and what to do next. 41	## Design Rule
42	
43	If a new concept does not improve one of the five verbs, it does not belong in EDF.
44	
45	The five verbs are:
46	
47	- Define
48	- Observe
49	- Explain
50	- Influence
51	- Validate

53	## Context Principle
54	
55	Every EDF analysis is valid only within its declared System Context.

60	
61	1. Define the System Context
62	   - Primary System
63	   - Context
64	   - Focus
65	2. Define the Outcome
66	3. Identify Manifestation(s)
67	4. Build the Origin Network
68	5. Trace Propagation
69	6. Evaluate Evidence

74	## Sequence Notes
75	
76	### 1. Define the System Context
77	
78	Every EDF begins by declaring its System Context.
79	
80	System Context has three required fields:
81	
82	- Primary System
83	- Context
84	- Focus
85	
86	These define what is being analyzed, what larger system materially influences it, and what aspect of the primary system is under examination.
87	
88	Different analyses may disagree partly because they declared different System Contexts. That is not automatically a conflict in evidence.
89	
90	### 2. Define the Outcome
91	
92	State the outcome in factual terms, not interpretive terms.
93	
94	Good:
95	
96	- Two aircraft were lost and the fleet was grounded
97	- The mission landed on the moon and returned safely
98	
99	Weak:
100	
101	- Management failed
102	- The launch culture was broken

104	### 3. Identify Manifestation(s)
105	
106	Manifestations are observable signals.
107	
108	They are how the outcome appears in the world. A complex outcome may have several manifestations.
109

111

113

115

117	- Human
118	- Organizational
119	- Environmental
120	- Financial
121	- Regulatory

134	- Financial

154	- Controllability
155	- Cost

221	CASE OD2-DEV2-NOCONC: Calderbridge night-rota pilot: falls rise at two care homes
222	
223	Setting: Larchmere Care Group runs nine residential care homes. Two homes in the town of Calderbridge, Ashby Fold (52 beds, two floors) and Penmor Lodge (44 beds, two floors), have piloted a reduced night-staffing rota since 1 June 2026. Group rollout of the rota to the other seven homes is planned for March 2027. You are the group quality lead, writing in mid-October 2026.
224	
225	Presenting request: The Director of Operations wants a recommendation for the 12 November 2026 board. Should the group put Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge back on four night staff and halt the March 2027 rollout of the pilot rota? What explains the rise in recorded falls at the two homes?
226	
227	INITIAL EVIDENCE
228	E1 [stage S1] Email from Marian Telfer, Director of Operations, to the group quality lead, 6 October 2026 (leadership-account): Subject: Calderbridge falls - board recommendation. Falls at our two night-rota pilot homes have nearly doubled: 16 in Q2, 31 in Q3 (Ashby Fold 9 to 17, Penmor Lodge 7 to 14). Since 1 June both homes have run nights with three staff (one carer per floor plus a floating senior) instead of four (two carers per floor). That is the obvious change. Night staff tell me they can't get to call bells as fast. We have no call-bell timings from before June, but I believe them. I want a recommendation for the 12 November board: put both homes back on four night staff now and pull the March rollout to the other seven homes. I am not prepared to wait another quarter.
229	E2 [stage S1] Group quality dashboard extract, Q3 2026, falls section (system-record): Recorded falls, Q2 to Q3 2026: Ashby Fold 9 to 17 (RED); Penmor Lodge 7 to 14 (RED); Brackenhill 11 to 9; Cresswell Court 8 to 9; Dunmore House 14 to 12; Elmstead 6 to 7; Fairholme 10 to 11; Greywater 12 to 9; Hatherley View 7 to 8. Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge combined, by month: Apr 4, May 5, Jun 7, Jul 11, Aug 9, Sep 11. RAG rule: red where the quarter-on-quarter rise exceeds 25%. Notes: figures are raw counts, not adjusted for occupancy. From 1 July, Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge incidents are imported directly from the Tallyline incident app. All other homes' figures are keyed in from paper incident forms by site administrators.
230	E3 [stage S1] Interview notes, night senior carers at Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge, 2-3 October 2026 (taken by the deputy quality lead) (staff-account): Ashby Fold night senior (9 years in post): 'With one carer per floor, if two bells go at once on the same floor somebody waits. We're slower, I'm sure of it, though I couldn't give you minutes.' Penmor Lodge night senior (in the floating role since June): 'It's different, not worse. Because I float, I'm usually free for the second bell. A lot of what's on the system now is people found sitting on the floor at the two o'clock check with no injury. We always had those. Whether they all got written up before, I honestly couldn't say.'
231	E4 [stage S1] Incident system query: falls by time of day, Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge combined, Q2 and Q3 2026 (system-record): Night (22:00-07:00): Q2 8, Q3 18. Day (07:00-22:00): Q2 8, Q3 13. Night share of falls: Q2 50%, Q3 58%. Day staffing at both homes did not change during either quarter. Source note: Q2 times come from paper forms. The time field was blank on 3 forms, and the administrator assigned those from the shift recorded. Q3 times are stamped automatically by Tallyline when the entry is made, which may be some time after the fall was discovered.
232	E5 [stage S1] Replies from the two registered managers to the Director of Operations, 7 October 2026 (manager-account): Penmor Lodge manager: 'I don't think it's the rota. Since Hollin Street Medical Practice took over our residents in May, the new GPs have been reviewing everyone's medication, and some residents have been started on night-time tablets. I'd look there first.' Ashby Fold manager: 'We moved to Hollin Street in May as well. My worry is admissions. We've taken more people from the hospital discharge-to-assess beds this summer, and they arrive frailer than our usual referrals. The rota is tight, but I'm not convinced it's the whole story.'
233	
234	EVIDENCE CATALOGUE (collect at most 3; read the file path to collect)
235	X1 [stage S1] Family complaints and compliments log, Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge, April-September 2026 - source: Group customer relations log (system-record) - file: evidence/X1.txt
236	X2 [stage S1] Night agency and bank shift usage, Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge, April-September 2026 - source: Group workforce and finance system (financial-record) - file: evidence/X2.txt
237	X3 [stage S1] Night staffing pilot protocol (approved April 2026) and status note, 3 October 2026 - source: Executive team papers (document) - file: evidence/X3.txt
238	X4 [stage S1] Monthly falls per 1,000 occupied bed days, all nine homes, January 2023-September 2026, with control limits - source: Group quality analyst, statistical chart pack (document) - file: evidence/X4.txt
239	X5 [stage S1] Infection-control and outbreak log, Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge, April-September 2026 - source: Group infection prevention lead (system-record) - file: evidence/X5.txt
240	X6 [stage S1] Nurse-call system export of night call response times, Ashby Fold, and nurse-call supplier note, Penmor Lodge - source: Nurse-call system export and supplier email (log) - file: evidence/X6.txt
241	X7 [stage S1] Tallyline implementation briefing to the group, May 2026 - source: Tallyline customer success manager, slide notes (vendor-account) - file: evidence/X7.txt
242	X8 [stage S1] Estates and maintenance log, Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge, April-September 2026 - source: Group estates helpdesk system (system-record) - file: evidence/X8.txt
243	X9 [stage S1] Most recent regulator inspection reports, Ashby Fold (March 2025) and Penmor Lodge (October 2024) - source: Care regulator public reports (regulator-record) - file: evidence/X9.txt
244	X10 [stage S1] Falls-prevention and moving-and-handling training records, Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge, 2026 - source: Group learning management system (system-record) - file: evidence/X10.txt
245	X11 [stage S1] Anonymous night-staff pulse survey, Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge, September 2026 - source: Trade-union branch survey (14 of 22 night staff responded) (anonymous-staff-survey) - file: evidence/X11.txt
246	X12 [stage S1] Post-fall observation completion audit, Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge, Q2 and Q3 2026 - source: Group clinical audit team (system-record) - file: evidence/X12.txt
247	X13 [stage S1] Director of Operations' memo to the executive team on the proposed night staffing pilot, 18 March 2026 - source: Executive team papers (leadership-account) - file: evidence/X13.txt
248	X14 [stage S1] Tallyline go-live record, falls by harm level Q2-Q3 2026, and Q2 handover-note cross-check, Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge - source: Deputy quality lead, compiled from Tallyline, paper forms and handover books (document) - file: evidence/X14.txt
249	X15 [stage S1] Clinical governance monthly packs, Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge, April-September 2026 - source: Registered managers' monthly governance returns (system-record) - file: evidence/X15.txt
250	
251	CANDIDATE HYPOTHESES
252	H1: The night-staffing pilot that began in June raised residents' underlying risk of falling at the two homes.
253	H2: The rise mainly reflects more complete recording of falls after the two homes switched to the incident app, rather than more falls actually happening.
254	H3: A shift in the resident population at the two homes toward frailer, higher-risk residents drove the rise.
255	H4: Underlying fall risk at the two homes did not change, and the Q3 figures are ordinary quarter-to-quarter variation for homes of this size.
256	H5: Prescribing changes made after the two homes moved to a new GP practice raised residents' fall risk.
257	
258	CANDIDATE CAUSAL LINKS
259	R1: Night-staffing pilot at the two homes (one carer per floor plus a floating senior) -> Higher recorded fall counts at the two homes in Q3 2026 (increases)
260	R2: Switch from paper incident forms to the incident app at the two homes -> Higher recorded fall counts at the two homes in Q3 2026 (increases)
261	R3: Change in resident mix toward frailer admissions at the two homes -> Higher recorded fall counts at the two homes in Q3 2026 (increases)
262	R4: Night-staffing pilot at the two homes -> Slower answering of night call bells (increases)
263	
264	CANDIDATE ACTIONS
265	A1: Return both homes to four night staff now and suspend the March rollout of the pilot rota to the other seven homes.
266	A2: Keep the pilot running under its existing pause criteria. Re-present falls as rates on the control chart with the change in reporting method marked, start manual sampling of night call-bell response times at both homes, and take the rollout decision at a dated review in late January using Q4 data.
267	A3: Issue formal capability warnings to the night senior carers at both homes over the rise in falls.
268	A4: Withdraw the incident app at the two homes and return them to paper forms until all nine homes can switch together, so that the dashboard compares like with like.
269	
270	SCORED ITEMS (answer every one)
271	Q01: hypothesis H1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
272	Q02: hypothesis H2 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
273	Q03: hypothesis H3 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
274	Q04: hypothesis H4 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
275	Q05: hypothesis H5 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
276	Q06: edge R1 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
277	Q07: edge R2 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
278	Q08: edge R3 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
279	Q09: edge R4 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
280	Q10: action A1 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
281	Q11: action A2 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
282	Q12: action A3 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
283	Q13: action A4 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
284	Q14: sufficiency SUFF allowed=[sufficient, insufficient]

# EDF Specification v0.3

Status: Working draft

This is the authoritative EDF v0.3 specification for the current draft.

Under EDF's constitutional version integrity rule, this defines a subsequent version rather than changing the meaning of v0.2 retroactively.

EDF evolves under constitutional rules defined in [constitution.md](constitution.md). The constitution governs framework evolution, not how to perform an EDF analysis.

## Purpose

EDF is a systems understanding framework with a diagnostic grammar.

It is used to explain how a system produced an outcome and to identify the highest-leverage opportunities for influencing future outcomes.

EDF is not primarily a decision framework. It establishes confidence in reality before decision frameworks such as Clarity evaluate what to do next.

Diagnostic Calibration is an optional extension for comparing, challenging, refining, and synthesizing multiple EDF analyses of the same system.

Framework changes should remain consistent with the constitutional rules of EDF.

## Design Rule

If a new concept does not improve one of the five verbs, it does not belong in EDF.

The five verbs are:

- Define
- Observe
- Explain
- Influence
- Validate

## Context Principle

Every EDF analysis is valid only within its declared System Context.

## Required Diagnostic Sequence

Every EDF analysis should follow this sequence:

1. Define the System Context
   - Primary System
   - Context
   - Focus
2. Define the Outcome
3. Identify Manifestation(s)
4. Build the Origin Network
5. Trace Propagation
6. Evaluate Evidence
7. Identify Control Points
8. Rank Control Points
9. Determine Diagnostic Sufficiency

## Sequence Notes

### 1. Define the System Context

Every EDF begins by declaring its System Context.

System Context has three required fields:

- Primary System
- Context
- Focus

These define what is being analyzed, what larger system materially influences it, and what aspect of the primary system is under examination.

Different analyses may disagree partly because they declared different System Contexts. That is not automatically a conflict in evidence.

### 2. Define the Outcome

State the outcome in factual terms, not interpretive terms.

Good:

- Two aircraft were lost and the fleet was grounded
- The mission landed on the moon and returned safely

Weak:

- Management failed
- The launch culture was broken

### 3. Identify Manifestation(s)

Manifestations are observable signals.

They are how the outcome appears in the world. A complex outcome may have several manifestations.

### 4. Build the Origin Network

Identify the contributing origins that made the outcome possible.

Origins may be:

- Technical
- Human
- Organizational
- Environmental
- Financial
- Regulatory

Complex outcomes should usually be modeled as an origin network rather than a single root cause.

### 5. Trace Propagation

Describe how effects moved from the origin network to the manifestations and outcome.

Propagation paths may be:

- Physical
- Informational
- Organizational
- Financial
- Human

### 6. Evaluate Evidence

Separate direct observation from inference.

Evaluate the quality of evidence supporting the current model and note meaningful gaps or disputes.

### 7. Identify Control Points

Identify where intervention could most effectively influence future outcomes.

Control points may differ from origins.

### 8. Rank Control Points

Rank candidate control points using:

- Influence
- Controllability
- Cost
- Confidence

The ranking does not need false precision. It does need a defensible ordering.

### 9. Determine Diagnostic Sufficiency

Ask:

> Do we understand enough to take the next responsible action?

Diagnosis is sufficient when additional investigation is unlikely to materially change the next responsible action.

## Required Output Elements

All EDF outputs should include, at minimum:

- System Context
- Primary System
- Context
- Focus
- Outcome
- Manifestation(s)
- Origin Network
- Propagation
- Evidence
- Control Points
- Control Point Ranking
- Confidence
- Diagnostic Sufficiency
- Unknowns
- Next Responsible Action

## Optional Extension: Diagnostic Calibration

Diagnostic Calibration is not required for routine EDF use.

Use it when:

- The situation is complex
- The stakes are high
- Causes are disputed
- Multiple disciplines are involved
- The cost of being wrong is significant

Diagnostic Calibration uses multiple independent EDF analyses to improve confidence in the diagnostic model while preserving valuable disciplinary perspectives.

See [diagnostic-calibration.md](diagnostic-calibration.md).

## Relationship To Complexity Levels

- Use [EDF-0](complexity-levels.md#edf-0-rapid) for rapid, low-complexity situations.
- Use [EDF-1](complexity-levels.md#edf-1-standard) when evidence and alternatives matter.
- Use [EDF-2](complexity-levels.md#edf-2-complex) when multiple interacting origins and layered control points must be modeled.

The sequence remains the same across levels. The depth changes.

## Relationship To Clarity

EDF creates the diagnostic grammar.

Diagnostic Calibration improves confidence in the diagnostic model.

Clarity uses the calibrated understanding to evaluate decisions.

Whether they all got written up before, I honestly couldn't say.'
E4 [stage S1] Incident system query: falls by time of day, Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge combined, Q2 and Q3 2026 (system-record): Night (22:00-07:00): Q2 8, Q3 18. Day (07:00-22:00): Q2 8, Q3 13. Night share of falls: Q2 50%, Q3 58%. Day staffing at both homes did not change during either quarter. Source note: Q2 times come from paper forms. The time field was blank on 3 forms, and the administrator assigned those from the shift recorded. Q3 times are stamped automatically by Tallyline when the entry is made, which may be some time after the fall was discovered.
E5 [stage S1] Replies from the two registered managers to the Director of Operations, 7 October 2026 (manager-account): Penmor Lodge manager: 'I don't think it's the rota. Since Hollin Street Medical Practice took over our residents in May, the new GPs have been reviewing everyone's medication, and some residents have been started on night-time tablets. I'd look there first.' Ashby Fold manager: 'We moved to Hollin Street in May as well. My worry is admissions. We've taken more people from the hospital discharge-to-assess beds this summer, and they arrive frailer than our usual referrals. The rota is tight, but I'm not convinced it's the whole story.'

CANDIDATE HYPOTHESES
H1: The night-staffing pilot that began in June raised residents' underlying risk of falling at the two homes.
H2: The rise mainly reflects more complete recording of falls after the two homes switched to the incident app, rather than more falls actually happening.
H3: A shift in the resident population at the two homes toward frailer, higher-risk residents drove the rise.
H4: Underlying fall risk at the two homes did not change, and the Q3 figures are ordinary quarter-to-quarter variation for homes of this size.
H5: Prescribing changes made after the two homes moved to a new GP practice raised residents' fall risk.

CANDIDATE CAUSAL LINKS
R1: Night-staffing pilot at the two homes (one carer per floor plus a floating senior) -> Higher recorded fall counts at the two homes in Q3 2026 (increases)

R4: Night-staffing pilot at the two homes -> Slower answering of night call bells (increases)

input.brief: The rise in falls at the two homes can't yet be pinned on the night rota. Three things changed at the same time: the rota (June), the incident app (July) and the GP practice and admission mix (May to summer). The app go-live matters most. Before July, falls came from paper forms. A check of Q2 handover notes found at least three unreported falls in just 6 of 13 weeks, and three more that might be falls. Unwitnessed "found on floor" falls rose from 5 to 14, mostly with no harm, which fits better recording. On the rate chart, both homes' Q3 rates are within their long-run ranges. Five other single-home rises of 70% or more in the group fell back without any action. That doesn't rule out a real rise, because the chart is slow to detect one. There are no call-bell times from before June, so slower answering can't be shown. My advice: keep the pilot under its pause criteria. Show falls as rates and mark the change in reporting method. Start manual sampling of night call-bell response times now. Review in late January with Q4 data. Don't issue capability warnings, and don't go back to paper. My confidence is moderate.
